description: Take a free 16-question DISC assessment with instant results and no email. Understand D, I, S, C, all 12 two-letter blends, and AI workplace prompts.
h1: Free DISC assessment (no email): how the 4 styles and 12 blends work.
dek: What Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness actually measure at work—and how to turn your score into team and AI instructions without an email gate.
lede: Most pages ranking for "free DISC test" let you click through 20–30 workplace adjectives and then lock your scores behind a work email or paid PDF report. AgentTune runs the open 16-item ODAT (Open DISC Assessment Test) completely inside your browser in about three minutes—zero email, zero signup—and pairs your score with MIT-licensed communication rules for teammates and AI assistants.
answer: You can take the free 16-question DISC test at agent-tune.com/tests/disc with instant browser-only scoring and no email required. Each of the four styles—Dominance (D), Influence (I), Steadiness (S), and Conscientiousness (C)—is scored from 4 to 20; if your second-highest style lands within 2 points of your top style, you get a two-letter blend like DC, DI, SC, or IS.

sections.h2: Take the 3-minute test or read the four quadrants first.
sections.html:
DISC maps workplace behavior across two everyday axes: Active / Fast-paced vs. Reserved / Methodical and Task-focused vs. People-focused. Ready to score yourself first? Start the free 16-item DISC test → (takes ~3 minutes, keyboard shortcuts 1–5).

StyleQuadrantDefault workplace preferenceWhat frustrates them in AI & meetings
D — DominanceFast-paced · Task-focusedBottom line first, clear tradeoffs, decision ownership.Throat-clearing intros, hedged non-answers, unrequested hand-holding.
I — InfluenceFast-paced · People-focusedBig-picture momentum, riffing out loud, crisp narrative framing.Dry walls of caveats that kill momentum before exploring options.
S — SteadinessMethodical · People-focusedPredictable step-by-step plans, calm pacing, clear impact on the team.Abrupt pivots, unflagged breaking changes, combative tone.
C — ConscientiousnessMethodical · Task-focusedPrimary sources, explicit assumptions, edge cases, exact numbers.Confident hand-waving, missing citations, glossed-over failure modes.

Few people sit purely in one corner. On our 16-item ODAT runner, when your runner-up quadrant finishes within 2 points of your highest total (for example, C = 17 and S = 16), your profile reports a two-letter blend. If two quadrants tie for first place, both styles are shown transparently rather than broken arbitrarily.

BlendWorkplace shorthandHow to tune your AI or team README
DC / CDArchitect-DriverLead with the conclusion, then back it immediately with numbers and failure modes; skip small talk.
DI / IDCatalyst-CloserOpen with the boldest high-leverage option and next action; keep energy high and prose tight.
DS / SDSteady ExecutorFocus on practical execution milestones, clear ownership, and realistic timelines.
IS / SICollaborative CoachUse a warm, constructive register; connect tasks to team impact and sequence changes smoothly.
IC / CIAnalytical StorytellerPair rigorous evidence with a clear executive narrative I can share with stakeholders.
SC / CSCareful Systems BuilderWalk through changes methodically, flag risks early, and verify edge cases before shipping.

Curious where frontier AI models land on the exact same 16 items? In our September 2026 benchmark, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1 all scored CS, while Grok 4.6 scored pure C (read the 5-model study).

sections.h2: Open ODAT vs. commercial workplace DISC assessments.
sections.html:
Transparency matters when using any personality questionnaire:

  • Not a clinical or hiring gate: ODAT is an open self-report adaptation from the Open Psychometrics Project (inspect all 16 items and JavaScript scoring code). Commercial assessments sold for HR workshops (such as Everything DiSC) use proprietary adaptive item banks and normed workplace reports—and should not be confused with an open 16-item self-reflection tool.
  • Why a 3-minute self-report works well for AI tuning: You do not need a psychometrically normed PDF to decide whether you want Claude or ChatGPT to lead with a 2-sentence bottom line (D) or a sourced verification checklist (C). Treat your DISC result as an editable draft of how you like information delivered.

sections.h2: Turn your DISC style into an AI prompt + team User Manual.
sections.html:
Here is a balanced DC (Dominance + Conscientiousness) communication block you can adapt for ChatGPT, Claude, Meta Muse, or AGENTS.md—or swap in all four pure styles in our DISC AI prompts guide:

## Working with me (DISC: DC — Direct & Analytical) - Bottom line first: state the recommendation or answer in sentence one. - Back claims with concrete evidence, tradeoffs, or primary sources—never filler adjectives. - Flag material uncertainty and unverified assumptions explicitly. - Push back directly if my plan has a cleaner, lower-risk alternative. - Default to tight prose; use tables when comparing 3+ options on shared criteria.

Want a version for human coworkers too? Drop your top 3 rules into our How to Work With Me card builder or copy the full Notion/GitHub layout in our How to Work With Me README template.

faq.q: Where can I take a truly free DISC test without giving my email?
faq.a: Go to agent-tune.com/tests/disc. All 16 ODAT questions run locally in your browser in about 3 minutes with zero email gate, account signup, or paywall.

faq.q: What do D, I, S, and C stand for in DISC?
faq.a: Dominance (direct, results-focused), Influence (outgoing, momentum-focused), Steadiness (patient, cooperative, methodical), and Conscientiousness (analytical, precise, evidence-driven).

faq.q: What does a two-letter DISC result like CS or DI mean?
faq.a: The first letter is your highest-scoring quadrant and the second letter is a close secondary style (within 2 points on the 4–20 ODAT scale) that shapes how you apply your primary style.

faq.q: Is the ODAT DISC test affiliated with commercial DiSC publishers?
faq.a: No. AgentTune uses the open 16-item ODAT adaptation for personal reflection and AI communication preferences; it is an independent self-report tool, not a commercial Everything DiSC assessment or hiring instrument.
